brief: The sixteenth statue holding a staff, a king's crown carved at her feet; Lubdhaka's foreman writing in his notebook; Dādī shaking her head gently and tapping the word; Śuka reading over his shoulder.
The twentieth statue holding a small carved lantern whose stone flame is steady; Dādī pointing at a row of three carved words on the plinth; Śuka squinting at them; the lamps of the hall flickering.

The nineteenth statue with a pale blue throat carved into the stone, a faint crescent moon over her brow; Dādī touching the throat and pointing outward; Śuka looking up the hall; Lubdhaka's foreman reading from his notebook.
A long garland of carved stone flowers laid along a table, each flower holding one tiny Sanskrit syllable-group; a brass lamp beside it; ink-and-watercolour illustration, soft ivory paper.
